AB01-q01-vnkrhg: Leaves out the emergency system, which uses parts of the service and parking systems to stop you if the brakes fail.
These are not the handbook's names; the 3 systems are service, parking and emergency.
AB01-q02-jxztdb: 100 psi is cut-in, where the compressor starts again; cut-out is around 125 psi.
150 psi is where the safety valve opens; the governor cuts out around 125 psi.
AB01-q03-j9b8hg: 55 psi belongs to the low-air warning range; the compressor cuts in around 100 psi.
75 psi is the top of the low-air warning range; cut-in is around 100 psi.
AB01-q04-v2exbq: Draining is not about pressure control; the governor handles that. You drain to remove water and oil.
The safety valve has nothing to do with draining; water and oil collect and the water can freeze.
AB01-q05-lfyb65: Too seldom; manual tanks must be drained at the end of each day of driving.
Water and oil build up in every season; drain manual tanks at the end of each day.
AB01-q06-rul2za: The evaporator only fights ice; you still drain daily to remove water and oil unless drains are automatic.
The evaporator puts alcohol into the air to prevent ice in cold weather, not to cool the compressor.
AB01-q07-eqivsz: 125 psi is governor cut-out; the safety valve usually opens at 150 psi.
100 psi is governor cut-in; the safety valve usually opens at 150 psi.
AB01-q08-d3hng8: A safety valve releasing air is never normal; something is wrong and a mechanic must fix it.
Cut-in happens around 100 psi and starts the compressor; it does not open the safety valve.
AB01-q09-qpsjnu: Pumping does not adjust the brakes; it only wastes air.
The governor's cut-out does not change; needless pumping just drains air faster than it is replaced.
AB01-q10-k3qh22: Wedge brakes are less common than S-cam brakes; the S-cam drum brake is most common.
Disc brakes are less common than S-cam brakes; the S-cam drum brake is most common.
AB01-q11-prhjq1: The power screw belongs to air disc brakes, not S-cam brakes.
Driving a wedge between the shoes is how wedge brakes work, not S-cam brakes.
AB01-q12-ywglj6: Braking harder feeds the fade; slow down and use a lower gear instead.
Pumping the brakes wastes air and does not cure fade; slow down and use a lower gear.
AB01-q13-u61gld: 20–45 psi is when spring brakes come fully on, not the warning range of 55–75 psi.
80–85 psi is the common setting on large buses; the required range is 55–75 psi.
AB01-q14-noisr0: 55–75 psi is the general required range; large buses commonly warn at 80–85 psi.
20–30 psi is the typical spring brake range, far below any low-air warning.
AB01-q15-78rfnu: Front wheel braking is good in all conditions; front skids are not likely even on ice. Keep it on "normal."
"Slippery" cuts front brake air pressure in half and reduces stopping power, loaded or empty; keep it on "normal."
AB01-q16-0nliyt: Low pressures get reduced front air; full front air comes only in hard stops of 60 psi or more.
Halving front air is what the manual "slippery" setting does; automatic valves give full air at 60 psi or more.
AB01-q17-mjxc4f: 55–75 psi is the low-air warning range; spring brakes come fully on at 20–45 psi.
100–125 psi is the governor's normal working band, not a spring brake range.
AB01-q18-3ukde9: Don't wait for the spring brakes; stop while you can still control the service brakes.
Pumping the pedal uses up air faster; it cannot build pressure. Stop safely right away.
AB01-q19-fc6az0: Pushing the yellow knob in releases the parking brakes; pull it out to set them.
The red 8-sided knob is the trailer air supply, and you never press the pedal with spring brakes on.
AB01-q20-w4jb60: Pressing the pedal does not release spring brakes; the danger is spring plus air force damaging the brakes.
The low-air warning depends on tank pressure; the real danger is damage from combined spring and air force.
AB01-q21-igoiki: To park you move the lever as far as it will go and lock it, not halfway.
Never press the brake pedal while spring brakes are on; just move the lever all the way and lock it.
AB01-q22-xhfclv: The separate tank only releases the spring brakes; it does not refill the main tanks.
Letting go of the spring-loaded valve puts the spring brakes back on, even with air in the separate tank.
AB01-q23-7gok6r: March 1, 1998 is the date for other air-brake vehicles; truck tractors date from March 1, 1997.
1975 relates to front brake limiting valves, not ABS; tractors need ABS from March 1, 1997.
AB01-q24-o3642e: This is true: ABS works only when wheels are about to lock, so it is not the false statement.
This is true: ABS helps you keep control in hard braking, so it is not the false statement.
